consensus_summary: Blind responses identify the primary and most common meaning of lamp oil as the Holy Spirit (indwelling, empowering, illuminating presence), especially via Matthew 25 and Zechariah 4, while listing common alternatives of readiness/watchfulness, good works/obedience, and faith/grace, plus minority views such as the Word of God or joy; no settled scholarly consensus exists beyond the popular primary reading.
book_summary: Oil is the commandment's truth and correction received and laid up inwardly until they govern the life—the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored as proven obedience; light is that obedience made visible as an example to others.
rationale: The book itself flags the Holy Spirit reading as the common teaching yet advances a different central claim that equates oil specifically with internalized commandments becoming Spirit-produced proven obedience. This displaces rather than matches or merely sharpens the dominant consensus identification of oil with the Spirit, even while borrowing elements from secondary alternatives (Word, works).
strongest_objection: The dominant popular and typological tradition (reflected in all three consensus responses) treats lamp oil as the Holy Spirit itself via Zechariah 4 and anointing parallels; equating it instead with stored obedience/fruit risks an idiosyncratic over-allegorization not required by the parable's readiness emphasis.
